plans.note: Primary text in sec-21 (Limitation of Liability); check the 'Excluded Claims' definition in sec-1 for the carve-out list and cross-check sec-20 indemnity for whether indemnities sit inside or outside the cap. Confirm mutuality, cap quantum vs. fees paid/payable, and exclusion of indirect damages.

sec-20 should contain the Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity; verify scope, defence/control, and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (data inputs/authorised use only). Cross-reference cap treatment in sec-21.

No dedicated heading; restrictions on our business lines or on buying/building competing products would most likely be buried in sec-12 (Customer Responsibilities), sec-2 (Scope) or sec-30 (General). Confirm absence before reporting.

Sole-source or exclusive-provider language typically appears in sec-2 (Agreement Structure and Scope) or sec-4 (Order Forms and Affiliate Orders); also check sec-12 for covenants not to procure comparable services elsewhere.

Direction-sensitive: an MFN would sit in sec-7 (Fees) or sec-4 (Order Forms). If it favours us, do not flag; only a Customer-side best-terms obligation is a deviation. Likely no such clause in this outline.
Non-solicit is commonly bundled into sec-30 (General) or sec-12; check duration, mutuality, employee scope and whether general advertising / unsolicited applications are carved out.

sec-9 (Termination) is primary; confirm Customer convenience right, notice length, absence of early-termination fees (check sec-7 and sec-10 for penalty/wind-down charges) and that Vendor has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.

sec-8 (Term and Renewal) should carry the auto-renewal mechanic and non-renewal notice window; check sec-7 for renewal price uplift. A missing reminder mechanic or uncapped uplift is a rationale note unless the window itself fails the fallback.

sec-28 (Governing Law and Dispute Resolution) is primary; confirm law is NY/DE/CA/E&W and forum is courts rather than foreign-seat arbitration. An accepted-but-not-preferred law is a rationale note only.

sec-24 (Assignment and Change of Control) is primary; verify our affiliate/successor assignment right without consent and that Vendor cannot terminate on our change of control. Check sec-30 for any residual assignment boilerplate.

sec-14 governs Deliverable ownership and sec-15 Customer Data; confirm no assignment or licence-back of our IP/data to Vendor beyond service provision, and check sec-13 licence scope and the sec-1 definitions of Deliverable / Customer Data / Vendor Technology.

sec-13 (Access Rights and Licence) is primary; test whether the grant extends to Affiliates and contractors, is non-revocable during the term, and is not limited by narrow user/site definitions in sec-1.

sec-22 (Audit Rights) is primary, with sec-23 (Records and Customer Assurance) as a related obligation; check frequency, advance notice, remote/off-site preference, business-hours limits and who bears cost.

Direction-sensitive: service credits in sec-3 running to us are acceptable and should not be flagged. Look for liquidated damages, penalties or interest payable by us in sec-7 (Fees/late payment) and sec-9/sec-10 (early termination charges).

sec-19 (Warranties) is primary; check warranty duration, whether the remedy is real (re-performance/refund) and how broadly disclaimers cut back. Cross-reference sec-6 (Acceptance) and sec-3 performance standards.
sec-18 (Insurance) exists; verify coverage lines and limits (including cyber/tech E&O given data handling under sec-15/sec-17) and certificate/notice obligations.
Look for committed spend, minimum volumes, non-reducible seat counts or true-up language in sec-7 (Fees) and sec-4 (Order Forms); confirm an exit or reduction right exists (cross-check sec-8/sec-9).

sec-11 (Transition Assistance and Data Return) is primary, with sec-10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) and sec-15 for data export/deletion; confirm duration of assistance, format of returned data and that assistance is available even on Vendor termination for cause.
